Newest first. Anything that moves a date or a deadline is also announced on ETL.

## 2026-11-24 — Final proposal: due Sunday 12/13, five pages, two panels

**The final proposal is now due Sunday 12/13 at 24:00**, not at the end of Week 15 (12/10). **It is five pages, references excluded**, not 8–10. It is still graded on the proposal rubric (§7.3), which has not changed.

**Week 16 (12/17) is now a panel discussion.** The twelve of you are split into two panels of six, and each panel discusses and evaluates its six proposals. Before the session you write a **peer review of each of the other five proposals in your panel**, using a short form: summary of the research objective, strengths and weaknesses on theoretical contribution and on practical significance, and an overall rating (Excellent, Very good, Good, Fair, Poor).

New on the [final proposal handout](handouts/final-proposal-guide.qmd): the page budget mapped to the rubric, a proposal template (HWP), and the peer review form in English and Korean.

Still to be posted: the panel assignments, the peer-review deadline, and the timing of the day.

## 2026-11-24 — No Discussant in Week 13 or Week 15

**심GS does not chair this Thursday (11/26), and 김SJ does not chair on 12/10.** The Discussant / Scribe role is dropped in both weeks. Nothing replaces it: the instructor chairs the open discussion, and **there is no 300-word synthesis due** for either week.

If you were listed as Discussant for one of these weeks, you have nothing to prepare and nothing to post. 심GS — this cancels the synthesis that the 11/24 entry below said was due 48 hours after class.

Everyone else is unaffected. Entry tickets are unchanged: one substantive question, 24 hours before class, from everyone not holding a role — which in these two weeks is six of you rather than five.

**Roster arithmetic.** Six weeks now run all seven roles and two run six, so the semester has **54 role slots** instead of 56. Discussant / Scribe is down to six slots for twelve people, so half the class will not hold it. 심GS and 김SJ each drop one turn. Everyone still holds Method Lead, Exemplar Analyst and Skeptic at least once, which was the one guarantee worth protecting.


## 2026-11-24 — No class on 12/3, and the data-driven week is cancelled

The building is closed on **Thursday 12/3** for 수시 면접 (admissions interviews), so **Week 14 has no class session**. Use that week to finish the final proposal, which is still due at the end of Week 15 (12/10). **Individual meetings on your proposal are available by appointment** — email the instructor; bring a draft.

That left one teaching slot before the defense (12/10) and two weeks wanting it. The slot stays with **Week 15, closing the horseshoe**, because the 12/17 defense is judged against exactly that material and it cannot usefully be taught after your proposal is written. So the **data-driven session (ML, computer vision, NLP) is cancelled, not rescheduled.** In its place:

- **Two required readings** for the 12/3 week — Shmueli (2010) and Kapoor & Narayanan (2023). These are the week's only reading.
- **One optional, ungraded exercise** — the planted-leakage dataset, posted on ETL, with no deadline.
- **A reference shelf** on the Week 14 page: the CV, NLP, prediction and sensor-fusion exemplars stay listed for anyone whose proposal needs them.

If your own proposal is ML-based, read the Week 14 page — it says plainly what you are not getting and what the readings do and do not cover.

**Role and assessment consequences.**

- Roles now run in **eight weeks, not nine** (W5–W8, W11–W13, W15): 56 slots, so **four to six turns** each instead of five or six. 최JM drops to three turns and 김DH loses the Discussant chair — if you lost a turn and want it back, say so.
- **배JH moves to Skeptic 2 in W15** (12/10), attacking El-Rayes & Kandil (2005), in the slot 최JM held. W14 was 배JH's only Skeptic turn, and everyone writes at least one referee report.
- **Graded Method Labs go from six to five** — Labs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6. The weight stays at 15%. The lab that was dropped is the leakage reproduction, which is now the optional exercise above rather than a deliverable due in proposal week.
- Week 15's in-class DSR lab is renumbered **Lab 9** so the numbering stays sequential.

## 2026-10-27 — Pre-proposal now due Sunday 11/1

**The pre-proposal (2 pages) is due Sunday 11/1**, not at the start of tonight's Week 8 session. You get five more days.

It no longer sits at the opening of a class, so nothing about Week 8 depends on it. The order is now: tonight's session (10/27), Dr. Kunhee Choi's lecture (10/29), your pre-proposal (Sun 11/1), then presentations (Tue 11/3).

One consequence worth planning around: there are now two days, not seven, between the proposals landing and the presentations. If you are reviewing a classmate's pre-proposal, you will be reading it over that weekend-to-Tuesday window.

## 2026-10-16 — Week 8 moves to Monday 10/26, a guest lecture lands on 10/29

**Three changes, and some dates move. Read this one.**

**Week 8 is now Monday 10/26 at 18:00**, not Tuesday 10/20. It is also a double session: survey measurement and quantitative modeling, which used to be two separate weeks, are now one — you build an instrument, then you model what it produces. Room announced on ETL.

**Week 9 (10/29) is a special lecture by Dr. Kunhee Choi**, "Making the most of your paper: what no one tells you!" No readings, no roles, no deliverable.

**Pre-proposal presentations move to Week 10 (Tue 11/3)**, and the response-to-reviewers letters that follow them are due in Week 11, now **Thursday 11/12**.

**Weeks 11 to 16 keep their numbers.** Week 11 also gains its Thursday back — it meets **11/12**, not Tuesday 11/10, because that Thursday turned out to be free after all. Weeks 12 to 16 are untouched.

Deadlines that moved:

- Pre-proposal due: Tue 10/20 → **Mon 10/26**, at the start of Week 8
- Pre-proposal presentations: 10/29 → **Tue 11/3**
- Week 11 and the response-to-reviewers letters: Tue 11/10 → **Thu 11/12**

What this costs, stated plainly: Delphi no longer has its own Method Lead — it stays on the reading list and in the framing segment, but nobody presents it. Lab 4 and Lab 5 both survive and are both still graded, but Lab 5 is now take-home, since two labs do not fit in one session. Six graded labs, unchanged.

**The role roster changed** for the merged week and in two other places. Merging two weeks removed seven role slots, so the roster was re-cut: W8's roles are now 김CG, 배JH, 이JW, 주JH, 박SJ, 김DH and 김NY. To keep everyone holding Method Lead, Exemplar Analyst and Skeptic at least once, 김CG takes a Skeptic turn in W11 and 김SJ takes one in W13. Everyone still has five or six turns, and nine Discussant slots for twelve people means three of you will not chair.

## 2026-10-02 — Week 5 exemplars replaced

**Week 5 has already met (10/1). Nothing you submitted for it needs redoing** — this change is for the record and for anyone returning to the week later.

The two exemplars for Week 5 are now:

- Tarekegn Gurmu, A., & Mahmood, M. N. (2024). "Critical factors affecting quality in building construction projects: Systematic review and meta-analysis." *JCEM*, 150(3) — a PRISMA systematic review, the design you drew a flow diagram for in Lab 1.
- Darko et al. (2020), unchanged — the scientometric side of the same question.

Zhao (2017) is dropped: its style of scientometric analysis no longer holds up well as a model. Javernick-Will & Scott (2010) stays on the page, but as a theory-driven study listed for reference rather than as the week's exemplar — it is not a clear model of problematization, which is what it was standing in for.

Problematization is now explicitly the framing segment and everyone's reading. The two role tracks for the week are the two ways of treating a literature as data: reviewing it systematically, and mapping it.

## 2026-09-17 — What each role holder prepares, week by week

Every role week in the [Weekly schedule](schedule.qmd) now opens with a **Roles this week** table: who holds each role, which method each Method Lead covers, which exemplar each Exemplar Analyst reads, and which exemplar each Skeptic attacks. Roles run in two tracks — Method Lead 1, Exemplar Analyst 1 and Skeptic 1 work one method and the paper that uses it; track 2 does the same for the other.

The Week 6 role walkthrough now uses this semester's actual Week 6 role holders instead of placeholder names.

Three conference dates collide with the seminar, on top of the Chuseok block already flagged for Week 4:

All four blocked sessions are made up. **Weeks 4, 10 and 13 run asynchronously with the role rotation intact** — if your turn falls in one of them you write the deliverable instead of presenting it, and it still counts as your turn. **Week 8 needs a live session**, because it is the pre-proposal presentations and peer review; the make-up date is being fixed and will be announced on ETL.

The response-to-reviewers letters, currently due in Week 10, respond to peer review from Week 8. That deadline follows the Week 8 make-up date and will be announced on ETL rather than moved quietly here.

Shifting the whole calendar back a week — listed as an option while Chuseok was the only conflict — is no longer viable. Four blocked Thursdays would push Week 15 past 12/10 into the exam period.

## 2026-09-04 — Week 2 required reading changed

The one reading to do if you do nothing else for Week 2 is now Halpin, D. W. (2007). "Fifty years of progress in construction engineering research." *JCEM*, 133(9), 635–639. It has been added to the Week 2 list.

Levitt (2007) stays on the list — it is still the forward-looking companion to Halpin's retrospective — but it is no longer the priority pick. If you already read Levitt after Week 1, nothing is wasted; read Halpin as well.

## 2026-09-02 — Week 2 preparation

Week 1 now ends with three things handed to you rather than none: your era team for the Week 2 workshop (drawn at random), the landmark works your team presents, and the JCEM volume you code in the Week 2 lab. Read them before Week 2 — the workshop is a prepared presentation, not an in-class reading session.

The landmark works are now named on the schedule with full citations — two per era, and three for 1955–75, where Gates (1967) and Carr (1982) are read against each other as a matched pair. All nine are journal papers.
